beta_new: Ease up simple rock to a ledge on the left, then follow the brown plated section, clipping two bolts; one more bolt sits on the final headwall.
Before reaching the high first bolt, you may be able to sling knobs and slot small cams.
Follow the series of cracks that slant rightward, clipping four bolts.
Begin to the right of the neighboring route, angling rightward to reach the northwest arete, which leads to a bolt; higher, traverse rightward over the west face to finish.
A single frustrating step reaches a tiny crystalline hole.

moves.from: Gear needed runs to about two inches, with tiny pieces up to an inch especially useful.

value.text: Gear runs to about two inches, with tiny pieces up to an inch especially useful.

beta_new: Ascend the scoop with minimal protection until a fixed piton on the right, then continue leftward and upward toward a bolt. One medium tricam can be placed between the two initial fixed points. Climb the chute directly as it gets steeper; mid-size Friends and tricams fit pockets on the unprotected stretch to the last bolt, and the belay is atop the Rappel Route.
Ascend the water-carved chute beside Lost Fortune on four bolts, carry on over the gentle face clipping two more, and a final bolt guards the overhanging step onto the summit.

Begin as the preceding route does, then work rightward to a bolted ledge. The next pitch, over 165 feet long, goes by six bolts up to a second belay station with bolts; to leave, traverse directly right.
Begin with a crack then clip four bolts above it, finishing at a bolt anchor.
Easy third-class scrambling except a roughly 10-foot flared chimney partway up, the only fifth-class section, which is much easier to downclimb than to climb.
Follow the dike on the adjacent rock behind, using its lone bolt, up to a bolted anchor for rappelling.
The southern top of the rock carries four bolts that serve as the toprope anchor.
Move up brown rock beside Dum Roodle's second pitch on its right, clipping five bolts and getting over several bulges. Rope drag is a consideration.
Step off a boulder to begin, and follow the edge up; a bolt appears about 20 feet up.
The crux is a hard, clumsy step to surmount a big bulge; this is the tallest line on the formation, with eight bolts to the anchor.
Stay along the arete's left side; past the third bolt, move rightward over the arete onto the slabbier rock.

Most parties stop after the fifth pitch and rappel, or add an extra pair of pitches and traverse to a neighboring route to rappel, or carry on to the upper ledges. Thin protection is needed on the upper section.
Angle up and rightward by two bolts, then step right into cracks of easier difficulty.
The hard moves are right at the start, as far as the third bolt; above that the climbing relaxes into easy ground to the anchors.
Follow the flake as it bends up toward the right, then continue by three bolts.
Set a toprope on the rust-hued arete beside the previous route, on its right; it merges with that route at the final bolt.
The start and finish are inelegant, while the middle part of the route is enjoyable and exposed.
The crack is deceptive; the hardest moves are in the first twenty feet.

moves.from: Gear needed up to about four inches.

value.text: Gear needed up to about four inches.

beta_new: Start with face moves past a bolt before reaching the crack.
Begin behind a tree, to the right side of B-Movie, in a crack that fades, then continue on the face by three bolts up to the summit.
Start up the right-facing corner on the left of the dike, then clip three bolts for the rest of the way.
Share the start with Marchesa but take the slim crack just to its right until it meets a horizontal one, jog rightward, and keep going in the slim crack higher up, passing one bolt.
The northeast side is the sole known line, with one bolt protecting it.
Four bolts lead to chain anchors. If a short runout above the ledge doesn't bother you, you can opt for the alternate anchors up and to the left.
Step off a 10-foot boulder and clip four bolts to reach grey flakes; a pair of extra bolts guard the face moves that lead to the summit.
Go up the boulder's southern face, clipping four bolts.
Small cams (TCUs) set in the corner offer backup for the second bolt's clip.
Past the fourth bolt, continue directly up the line by two more bolts. A big move comes close to the top.
Start from the short crack that slants on the right, then continue up past the two bolts.
Take the lower half of the neighboring route to a right-hand ledge, then work the face above on a trio of bolts plus a hidden pin.
A full pitch with plenty of excitement near the top. A short alternate start called Sidesaddle joins in.

moves.from: ; bring cams in the number 2 to number 3 size for the crack

value.text: Bring cams in the number 2 to number 3 size for the crack.

beta_new: Clip a bolt near the start, then climb dark stone up to the ledge. Above the ledge, follow cracks and then three bolts leading to the top.

Start up the crack beside a black streak on its left, then traverse right by a bolt, reaching a dihedral that has a ledge. Standing on that ledge, angle up leftward along a crystal-studded ridge, passing a bolt, to arrive at a shallow crack.
Follow the thin seam up the smooth pale slab, which holds four bolts.
Leave the boulder at the corridor entrance and angle rightward by a bolt to reach a long crack that goes straight in.
